questions.q: Why does this lesson say declaring a separate variable for each item (customer1, customer2, customer3...) doesn't scale?
options: Apex has a strict limit of exactly two variables per class
It makes looping over the items impossible, since a loop needs one name it can refer to repeatedly, not a different name for every item
Apex does not allow more than one variable to hold a String
It causes a compile-time error after exactly three variables
questions.explain: The lesson's core argument for collections is that separate per-item variables can't be looped over, since a loop needs a single name to refer to repeatedly -- which is exactly what a collection provides.

questions.q: In a List with 3 items, what is the index of the last item, and why?
options: 3, because indexing starts at 1
2, because List indexing starts at 0, so the last valid index is always size() - 1
4, because Apex always reserves one extra index
There is no last index in a List
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly states indexing starts at 0, so with 3 items at indexes 0, 1, and 2, the last valid index is size() - 1 = 2; accessing index 3 would throw a runtime error.

questions.q: What happens when you call `.add('Prospecting')` on a Set that already contains the value 'Prospecting'?
options: The Set throws a compile-time error
The duplicate add is ignored -- a Set does not allow duplicate values, so the Set's size does not increase
The Set automatically converts itself into a List
The existing 'Prospecting' value is removed from the Set
questions.explain: The lesson's example shows adding 'Prospecting' twice to a Set results in a size of 2, not 3 -- the duplicate add is silently ignored because Sets disallow duplicates.

questions.q: Per this lesson, when is a Map the right collection to reach for?
options: Whenever duplicate values must be strictly forbidden
Whenever you need to look values up quickly by a known key rather than scanning through items by position
Whenever order matters more than anything else
Only when working with Integer values
questions.explain: The lesson frames a Map as the right tool whenever you need to look something up by a known identifier (key) rather than scanning an entire List checking each item by position -- like looking up loyalty points by customer name.

questions.q: According to this lesson's decision guide, which collection should you use if you care about order and need to allow duplicate values?
options: Set
Map
List
None of Apex's collection types support duplicates
questions.explain: The lesson's decision guide is explicit: if you care about order and allow duplicates, use a List; a Set disallows duplicates, and a Map is for key-based lookup rather than ordered sequences.
